title: Determination 2023/033: Compliance of, and decisions made by an authority in relation to, building work encroaching on to a neighbouring property
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Christchurch City Council as building consent authority; MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992). C/AS1 for Sleeping (residential) and Outbuildings (risk group SH): Amendment 3 (effective 1 July 2014 to 30 May 2017, current at the original consent of 4 August 2015) and Amendment 4 (effective 1 January 2017 to 3 November 2021, current at the third amendment) (p.30 fn 34).
document_date: 7 December 2023 (clarified under s 189; first issued 10 November 2023, per p.1 fn 1)

facts.text: Earthquake-damaged elements of a concrete driveway and parking bay, a concrete block retaining wall and a timber vehicle deck were repaired or rebuilt on a residential property. Some elements were built across the boundary onto the neighbouring property.

The neighbouring owner disputes the compliance of the work with B1, B2 and C3 Fire affecting areas beyond the fire source, and disputes several authority decisions: the building consent, a third amendment, the code compliance certificate, and an alleged failure to issue a notice to fix.
The determination consulted Fire and Emergency New Zealand under section 170 on matters concerning fire safety.
The applications for the original consent and the third amendment did not indicate a proposed means of compliance with clauses C1 to C6 Protection from Fire.
The authority's letter of 9 August 2016 said the work would not comply with clause C where it encroaches on other property. The authority later issued a code compliance certificate on 13 August 2018.

The applicant's position is that fire spread is not limited to encroachment, that elements closer than 1.0 m need fire resistance above the 30-minute residential minimum, and that the authority did not show how C3 was met.
Functional requirement C3.3 reads: buildings must be designed and constructed so there is a low probability of fire spread to other property vertically or horizontally across a relevant boundary.
Other evidence considered includes an expert report that concluded the work complied with B1, B2 and C3, and the consent drawings and photographs of the timber vehicle deck.
